requires.label: Must be a Colorado resident
requires.quote: An individual must be a Resident of Colorado in order to qualify for Financial Assistance.

rules.label: Financial Assistance Based on Family Income - 100% discount
rules.quote: The Patient is Uninsured or Under-insured; and Guarantor's annual Family Income ("Family Income") is not more than four hundred percent (400%) of the current federal poverty level (FPL) guidelines.

rules.label: Financial Assistance Based on Family Income - discounted
rules.quote: The Patient is Uninsured or Under-insured; and Guarantor's annual Family Income ("Family Income") is not more than four hundred percent (400%) of the current federal poverty level (FPL) guidelines.

rules.label: Catastrophic Balance Financial Assistance
rules.quote: The Patient's outstanding single account balance due after all insurance or third-party payments and/or discounts (including the application of Financial Assistance based on family income alone) is greater than 50% of the Patient's total annual Family Income and Financial Resources combined.

rules.label: Presumptive Eligibility for Financial Assistance
rules.quote: Presumptive eligibility for Financial Assistance may be granted for circumstances outlined in the Presumptive Eligibility section of this policy.

application.quote: Applicants have the later of (a) 365 days from the date of the first post-discharge Billing Statement, or (b) 30 days after notice of the initiation of one or more Extraordinary Collection Actions ("ECA") has been provided, to submit an application or to request a reconsideration of an incomplete and denied application

eca_not_before.quote: UCHealth does not initiate ECAs prior to (a) 365 days from the date UCHealth provides the first post-discharge Billing Statement to the Patient; and (b) reasonable efforts have been made to determine whether a Guarantor is approved for Financial Assistance under this policy, as described in this section.

notes: For unscheduled emergency services, UCHealth may, at its sole discretion, make an exception to the residency requirement.

UCHealth employees residing outside the State of Colorado, but who receive services at a UCHealth facility do not have to meet residency requirements for financial assistance applications they may request.
UCHealth will not participate in or support any activities (including facilitating media access) related to fundraising efforts intended to pay for a specific patient's care.
UCHealth's Financial Assistance Program is not responsible for providing housing, food, transportation, immigration status, or continuity of care to any individual.
UCHealth is available to help identify community-based resources, facilitate services, and provide appropriate referral assistance.

UCHealth acts in accordance with the Federal Consolidated Appropriations Act of 2021 No Surprises Act under title I and Transparency under title II as well as the Code of Federal Regulations Internal Revenue Service Exempt Organizations rules 26 CFR 1.501(r)-0 through 26 CFR 1.501(r)-7.
Services provided at UCHealth clinics both inside and outside of Colorado are eligible for UCHealth Financial Assistance.
Patients with UCHealth debt are not denied services for non-emergency care and are not excluded from financial assistance.
Some services provided by physicians at UCHealth facilities may or may not be covered by the UCHealth Financial Assistance Policy (FAP).

Care and expenses not covered by the FAP: Health care services that are not emergent or Medically Necessary ("Medically Necessary"), including elective or cosmetic surgery; and Health care services related to a transplant procedure, self-pay package, single case agreement, grants & research, or when there is a legal obligation for a third party (i.e. certain individuals, entities, insurers or programs) to pay a claim.

If Family Income is at or below 250% of FPL, Financial Assistance is valid for 365 days from the date of the last signed and dated Financial Assistance Application. Patients must re-submit an application for Financial Assistance if more than 365 days has passed from the last signed and dated Financial Assistance Application.

If Family Income is between 251-400% of FPL, eligibility for Financial Assistance is valid for 180 days from the date of the last signed and dated Financial Assistance Application. Patients must re-submit an application for Financial Assistance if more than 180 days has passed from the last signed and dated Financial Assistance Application.

If UCHealth determines that an individual is approved for Financial Assistance following UCHealth's review of a complete application, UCHealth will reverse ECAs (if any) and will refund amounts previously paid for care covered by this policy in excess of the amount owed, except overpayments that are $1 or less. If the Guarantor still owes any amount, UCHealth will provide an updated Billing Statement showing how the adjusted amount was determined.
Information from the predictive model may be used to determine presumptive eligibility for Financial Assistance when the estimated household FPL is reported to be 250% or less.
Presumptive eligibility for Financial Assistance will only apply to current services and past accounts. Presumptive eligibility does not extend to future services.

UCHealth will not charge Patients approved for Financial Assistance more than the amount generally billed (AGB) by UCHealth to insured Patients for emergency or Medically Necessary care covered by this policy.
If the self-pay discount for a hospital facility is greater than AGB, a discount equal to the self-pay discount will be applied to gross charges to a Patient approved for Financial Assistance.
UCHealth will seek payment on accounts with balances in self-pay (i.e., Patient liability). UCHealth initiates ECAs only when permissible, including legal action and wage garnishment.

UCHealth will provide any itemized statement requested by a Guarantor, in compliance with Colorado law, either within: 10 business days of the request; 30 days after discharge for inpatients; or 30 days after the service is rendered for outpatients, whichever is later.

UCHealth will make reasonable efforts to determine whether an individual is FAP-eligible for care provided by UCHealth by: Making a reasonable effort to provide oral notification to individuals, at least 30 days prior to initiating an ECA, about the FAP and how to obtain assistance with the application process; Providing a written notice to Patients at least 30 days prior to initiating an ECA indicating that Financial Assistance is available to eligible Patients, identifying the ECAs that UCHealth intends to initiate, and stating a deadline after which ECAs may be initiated that is no sooner than 30 days after the date the written notice is provided; and Including a FAP Plain Language Summary with the notice described above in the above Section titled Financial Assistance Policy and Application Availability.

UCHealth will send at least four (4) monthly Billing Statements, mailed every thirty (30) days, to the Guarantor of an account informing of a balance due with an address in the United States, Canada or Mexico.
After UCHealth has sent four (4) Billing Statements and received no payment and no application within thirty days of the final Billing Statement, UCHealth may refer the account to collections.
All parties engaged in collection actions on behalf of UCHealth will be required to follow this policy, including contracted collection agencies.
Patient debt with UCHealth is not reported to credit agencies nor are liens placed on the patient's property.

The UCHealth Financial Counseling department will have final authority to decide whether UCHealth has made reasonable efforts to determine whether a Patient is eligible for Financial Assistance under this policy, and therefore whether UCHealth may engage in ECAs against the Guarantor.
